insights.title: Your BMI is just above the Asian action point
insights.why: It is above 23.0, the WHO public-health action point for Asian populations.
insights.means: This is informational only and not a label of overweight; our rule proposes no test. Your waist is below the Asian-Indian male cut-point, and your heart-health habits score gives BMI 100.
insights.do: Nothing to change on this alone.
insights.expected: Keep an eye on it at your yearly check.

insights.title: Your father's diabetes makes yearly sugar checks worthwhile
insights.found: Your father developed type 2 diabetes at 52.
insights.why: Family history is one of the strongest pointers for diabetes; your own HbA1c (5.45%), fasting glucose (88 mg/dL) and fasting insulin (6.1) are all in range.
insights.means: Your sugar control is good now. The family history is a reason to keep a baseline, not a diagnosis.
insights.do: Keep HbA1c in your yearly tests.
insights.expected: An early signal if anything changes.

insights.title: Your heart markers are good, with one family pointer
insights.found: Your paternal grandfather had a heart attack at 68. Your ApoB is 82 mg/dL, LDL 2.6 mmol/L, HDL 1.4, triglycerides 82 mg/dL and blood pressure 118/76.
insights.why: None of your heart markers is flagged by the lab or by our rules.
insights.means: Lp(a) 45 nmol/L is within the lab's range (<75). It was reported in nmol/L, which cannot be converted to mg/dL, so our rules could not read it; it does not need repeating.
insights.do: Nothing to do now. A first heart-risk estimate needs your total cholesterol on the panel.
insights.expected: A baseline to compare against in future.

insights.title: Your omega-3 index is below the lab's target
insights.found: Omega-3 index 6.5% on 18 Oct 2026; the lab prints a target above 8%.
insights.why: No rule in our library reads this test, so it is shown as reported.
insights.means: It reflects how much omega-3 fat is in your red cells. Our research did not assess it for you.
insights.do: Discuss with your doctor whether it matters for you.

insights.title: Your wearable shows a fit, steady pattern
insights.found: Over 7 days: resting heart rate about 56, HRV about 62 ms, about 10,050 steps a day, 7.2 hours of sleep, and an estimated VO2max of 47.5.
insights.why: These are consumer-device estimates, summarised as averages.
insights.means: They fit your reported 210 minutes a week of running and resistance training. Device numbers are trends, not lab measurements.
insights.do: Keep wearing it; your twin can follow the trend.
insights.expected: A baseline your twin can compare against.

insights.title: Four more results would give your biological age
insights.found: PhenoAge needs nine blood results. You have five: creatinine, glucose, CRP, MCV and RDW.

insights.means: We never estimate a biological age from missing values.

glossary: PhenoAge
A published biological-age method (Levine 2018) that combines nine blood results with your age. Research use only.
HbA1c
Average blood sugar over about the last 2-3 months.
ApoB
A count of the particles that carry cholesterol into artery walls.
Lp(a)
Lipoprotein(a): a cholesterol particle whose level is mostly inherited; measured once in a lifetime.
hs-CRP
High-sensitivity C-reactive protein: a blood marker of inflammation.
BMI
Body mass index: weight divided by height squared.
eGFR
Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
Rule
One of our clinical checks. Each has a source, a threshold and an evidence grade; it fires only when your result clears it.
HRV
Heart rate variability: the beat-to-beat variation in your heart rhythm, measured by your wearable.
Omega-3 index
The share of omega-3 fats in your red cell membranes.
